title: Highest Point of the Ride
statement:
A bike ride passes through n + 1 checkpoints. It starts at checkpoint 0 at altitude 0. You get an array gain of length n, where gain[i] is the change in altitude from checkpoint i to checkpoint i + 1. It can be negative.

Return the highest altitude reached at any checkpoint, including the starting one.

examples.why: The altitudes are 0, -3, 2, 4, -2, 2. The biggest single climb is 5, but it starts from -3, so the peak is 4.
The ride only goes down. The start, at 0, is the highest point.

hints: The altitude at each checkpoint is the sum of all gains before it.
Keep a running total and remember the largest value it ever takes. Do not forget the starting altitude of 0.

explain.intuition:
The altitude at checkpoint i is the sum of the first i gains: a prefix sum. You want the largest prefix sum, where the empty prefix (the start, 0) also counts.

You do not need to store all the altitudes. Walk once, add each gain to a running altitude, and keep the best value seen.
steps: Set alt = 0 and best = 0. The start is a checkpoint.
For each g in gain, add it to alt and set best = max(best, alt).
pitfalls: Starting best at gain[0] or at -Infinity. When every gain is negative, the answer is the starting 0.
Returning the largest single gain instead of the largest running sum.

solutions.title: Build every altitude
solutions.idea: Write out the altitude of all n + 1 checkpoints, then take the maximum.

solutions.title: Running altitude
solutions.idea: Track the current altitude and the best one so far in a single pass.

followups: Return the biggest total climb between any two checkpoints, where the later one is higher. How does that relate to a single stock trade?
Answer many queries of the form "altitude at checkpoint i" in O(1) each.
